draft.title: Steam power and new inventions
card: Steam engine
A machine that burns coal to heat water and make steam, which drives moving parts. Thomas Newcomen built an early engine to pump water out of mines. James Watt later improved it so it used less coal.
Machines

Spinning machines such as the spinning jenny made thread faster than hand spinning. Power looms wove thread into cloth. Later, steam could drive them, so work was no longer tied to rivers or to hand tools.
Railways
Steam locomotives ran on iron rails. Early lines carried coal, and by the 1830s trains carried goods and passengers between Britain's towns and ports.
Together these changed how goods were made and moved. Machines made large amounts of cloth and other goods quickly. Railways carried them to buyers far away.
draft.remember: Steam engines and machines changed how goods were made. Railways changed how they were moved.

a.q: What was the main effect of spinning and weaving machines on how cloth was made?
opts: Large amounts were made much faster than by hand
Cloth was made only in people's homes
Less thread was needed to make each metre
Cloth could be made without any workers
a.why: Machines spun thread and wove cloth far faster than hand work, so much more cloth was made. Machines still needed workers to run them, so the option about no workers is wrong.
a.clue: Think about speed compared with hand spinning.

b.q: A mill owner in Lancashire in the 1830s wants to sell cloth in a port town far away. Which invention most directly helps him move it there?
opts: The steam locomotive on iron rails
The spinning jenny
The power loom
Watt's improved steam engine
b.why: Locomotives on railways carried goods between towns and ports, so they changed how goods were moved. The spinning jenny and power loom helped make thread and cloth, not move it. Watt's engine mainly made power more efficient.
b.clue: Which invention is about moving goods, not making them?

a.best: Large amounts were made much faster than by hand

b.best: The steam locomotive on iron rails

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and the only one with an added detail ('on iron rails'), and it is the only transport option, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.
